info.desc: "Led Zeppelin IV" is the common, but unofficial name of the untitled fourth album of English rock band Led Zeppelin. It was released on November 8, 1971. It has no official title printed anywhere on the album, but is generally called "Led Zeppelin IV" after the band's previous three numbered albums. Atlantic Records catalogs have used the names "Four Symbols" and "The Fourth Album"; it has also been referred to as Zoso, which the first symbol appears to spell. podcast.body: In the 1990s, a copy of Led Zeppelin's fourth album, which includes "Stairway to Heaven," was observed selling for $24.99 on CD. This price was equivalent to nearly $40 in contemporary money, significantly more expensive than the vinyl version which could be purchased for around $6.99 on sale, despite the album having already sold over 20 million copies and having long recouped its costs. "I recall being in a store in the 90s and seeing a copy of Led Zeppelin's fourth album, you know, in the one with the stairway to heaven on it. Selling for $24.99."

podcast.body: This album was notable for its almost complete lack of traditional liner notes, a deliberate choice to build mystery and myth around the band. The cover featured no title and the band's name was absent. The gatefold sleeve contained only a painting of "the Hermit" figure. Basic information and four unique "root symbols" representing each band member were found only on the inner paper sleeve, alongside minimal song lyrics. "Led Zeppelin's fourth album had almost zero in the way of liner notes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was recorded using the Rolling Stones Mobile Recording Studio, which was parked outside Headley Grange, and features iconic tracks such as "Stairway to Heaven," "Black Dog," and "Rock and Roll." "The Zeppelin used the Rolling Stones mobile to record no fewer than four albums, including their Led Zeppelin four album with stairway to heaven and black dog and rock and roll on it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
